full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman J : This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and opposite party No. 1 Mr. Harunar Rashid Chowdhury, Joint Director, Banking Control Department, Bangladesh Bank, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka to show cause why petitioner Mustafizur Rahman, Chairman and Managing Director of Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Limited (hereinafter referred to as BCI Limited) as well as a member of the Parliament should not be enlarged on bail in Motijheel PS Case No. 12 (8) 92 corresponding to GR Case No. 4203 of 1992 under sections 403/406/409/109 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The facts leading to the present case are as follows : Accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman, B Corn, joined the then United Bank Limited (now called the Janata Bank) as an officer Grade-III in the year 1966, continued to serve in the Janata Bank till 25.4.83 and was lastly posted as Manager (Senior Principal Officer) in Grade-I in Dhaka. He resigned from the service of the said nationalised bank and joined the National Bank Limited (a private bank) on 26.4.83 as an Assistant Vice-President. Subsequently he became its Vice-President with effect from 1.1.86 and served till 8.1.87. It appears from the papers submitted by the Bangladesh Bank before this Court that accused petitioner Mustafizur Rahman although served in the National Bank Limited till 8.1.87, yet at the same time he served as Adviser to the Board of Directors of BCI Limited since its inception in 1985-86. It also further appears that the Board of Directors of BCI Limited appointed accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman as the President and Managing Director of BCI Limited in its meeting dated 4.10.86 and the said fact was informed to the Governor, Bangladesh Bank by their letter dated January 13, 1987. 

 ii) The company will not handle Letter of Credit business or Wage Earners remittance. However, in the case of foreign currency loan syndicated by the company, they may handle Letter of Credit business to the extent of such loans with prior clearance from Exchange Control Department of Bangladesh Bank in each case. 

 8. Another news item appeared in 'The Daily Star' dated April 24, 1992 that—BCI Limited has become inoperative due to (illegal) over-drawing of company funds by its directors, that (illegal) funneling of funds from the investment company BCI Ltd, (by the accused and his associates), set up seven years ago by them created the liquidity crisis, paralysing its operations, that the depositors will never be able to get back any part of their deposits as only in case of regular banks the Bangladesh Bank can pay the depositors upto 60% of their deposits and that when the Chairman and Managing Director of BCI Limited Mr. Mustafizur Rahman (accused-petitioner) was contacted, he acknowledged the liquidity crisis of his company. The Bangladesh Bank by its order dated 28.4.92 suspended the activities of the BCI Limited. It is interesting to note that although BCI Limited is neither a Nationalised Bank nor a private bank yet the Manager of the Green Road Branch (Dhaka) had the courage to write illegally to the Registrar of this Court its letter dated 9-4-91 that as various Government, Semi-Government and private institutions have been depositing money with the BCI Limited and as BCI Limited does not deduct levy or surcharge from the interest earned and also gives various other facilities the money lying with the Supreme Court in the fund of its Original Side should be deposited with the Green Road Branch of the BO Limited and thereafter between 28-4-91 at22-8-91 Tk. 54,32,651.00 from the Admiralty Suit No. 2 of 1971 and further amount of Tk, 1,49,08,805.00 from the fund of various companies in liquidation from the Supreme Court Branch of the Sonali Bank, Malakatola Branch of the Krishi Bane in Matter Nos. 21/1978, 27/1978 and 29/1982 were withdrawn and deposited by the order of the relevant Bench dated 2.7.91, 29.5.91, 28.4.91 and 22.8.91 in the Green Road Branch of BCI Limited although it is not a Bank. The Registrar, Supreme Court subsequently by his two letters dated 21.4.92—one addressed to the Manager of the Green Road Branch of BCI Limited and another addressed to accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman, Chairman and Managing Director of BC! Limited Head Office, Taranga Complex, 19 Rajuk Avenue, Motijheel, Dhaka in pursuance of the order of the successor Judge of the Admiralty-cum-Company Bench of the High Court Division (apparently realising the illegality and urgency) asked to refund the deposit No. 17588/34 dated 5.7.91 to this Court by pay order, draft or cheque with interest immediately but neither the said Manager nor the accused-petitioner Managing Director and Chairman of BCI Limited gave any reply to the same. Thus apparently Tk. 2,03,41,456.00 of the Original Side of this Court was also dishonestly misappropriated by the Managing Director and his associates as bankers. This is a matter on record in this Court. 

 9. In the daily newspaper, namely, the "Morning Sun" dated April 29, 1992 a report of its reporter was published to the effect that the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka issued warrants of arrest against all the Directors of BCI Limited for conducting unauthorised banking transactions following a case filed by the Bangladesh Bank being Case No. 382 A-1 of 1992 under sections 109 and 111 of the Banking Companies Act, 1991 against accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman and 19 other Directors of BCI Limited. The BCI Limited is said to have failed to keep reserve liquid asset to the minimum extent of 10% of their total liabilities in violation of clause 8 of Non-Banking Financial Institution Order, 1989, grant of unauthorised commercial loan against lien of balances in investment account, operating current account like a commercial schedule bank, allowing interests on deposits holding investment account, advancing loan of huge amount of Tk. 18,78,00,000.00 (Taka eighteen crores seventy-eight lacs) in the benami of the relations of the Directors as on 31.12.90. In the said case accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman was taken into custody on 12.5.92 by a Division Bench of this Court refusing to grant anticipatory bail, but subsequently the accused-petitioner succeeded in getting an order of bail from another Division Bench of this Court on 27.7. 92 in Criminal Miscellanous Case No. 295 of 1992 arising out of the complaint case filed by the authorised officer of the Bangladesh Bank against the accused-petitioner and other Directors in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 11. It appears that the BCI Limited as petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 1730 of 1992 against the order of Bangladesh Bank dated 28.4.92 suspending all the operations of the petitioner BCI Ltd with immediate effect till inquiry. The said writ petition was heard at length by a Division Bench of this Court for 5 days and was rejected on June 18, 1992 (after hearing both the parties with the direction that the inquiry in the affairs of the BCI Limited is to continue and the function of BCI Limited as a bank is to remain suspended till inquiry which should be completed at an early date in public interest. On behalf of the Bangladesh Bank (i.e. opposite party No. 1) papers have been placed before this Court to show that enquiry is continuing and that some of the Directors and their relations took a huge sum of Tk. 18,78,00,000.00 as loan in patent violation of Articles 51 and 52 of Articles of Association as well as section 86 (D) of the Companies Act, 1913 and misappropriated the said amount of money and that the accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman as Managing Director and Chairman accepted the resignation of these Directors collusively without trying to recover the said amounts of money from them by filing civil suits, criminal cases, etc. against them. (This fact was also stated by the Bangladesh Bank in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 295 of 1992 and also in Writ Petition No. 1730 of 1992). 

 12. In the present case which has been filed after completing part of the enquiry OP No. 1 Harunar Rashid Chowdhury, Joint Director, Banking Control Department, Bangladesh Bank, head Office, Dhaka as informant lodged FIR with Motijhecl PS on 8.8.92 (giving rise to Motijheel PS Case No. 12 dated 8.8.92) against accused Mustafizur Rahman and 10 others (as his accomplices) stating that on the order of accused Mustafizur Rahman an amount of Tk.60 lacs of BCI Limited was given in the name of the petitioner's employee Circulation Manager co-accused Manjur Abedin Chowdhury of accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman's own weekly 'Sandwip' without any security as a clean loan, that the said weekly 'Sandwip' is owned by accused Mustafizur Rahman, that accused Mustafizur Rahman dishonestly misappropriated the said amount of Tk. 60 lacs of the BCI Limited after having got dominion over the said amount of money by withdrawing it in the benami of his said employee. It has been further stated in the FIR by the informant that accused Mustafizur Rahman, with the intention of dishonestly misappropriating the money of BCI Limited gave Tk. 3 lacs in the name of loan in the benami of his accomplice Mozammel Hossain, Chairman of Haramiah Union Parishad, Sandwip on 31.3.91 and having thus got dominion over the said amount of Tk. 3 lacs of the BCI Limited dishonestly misappropriated the said amount of Tk. 3 lacs. Informant further stated in the FIR that on inquiry he further found that on 12.12.91, 22.12.91, 24.12.91 and on 30.12.91 accused Mustafizur Rahman in total dishonesty withdrew Tk. 12.50 lacs from Moulvi Bazar Branch (Dhaka) of BCI Limited by telephonic direction through the Vice-President of the said Branch namely, co-accused Shahabul Hussain diverting the same from deferred accounts and himself dishonestly misappropriated the said amount of money of BCI Limited. Informant also stated that accused Mustafizur Rahman himself dishonestly, misappropriated Tk. 6,15,000.00 on 24.12.91 from the said Moulvi Bazar Branch (Dhaka) of BCI Limited by approving the diversion of the said money from the business development fund through 3 vouchers with the help of said co-accused Shahabul Hossain. The informant further stated that accused Mustafizur Rahman between 1.1.92 and 21.4.92 from the Khulna Branch of BCI Limited dishonestly misappropriated Tk. 13,51,119.00 withdrawing the said amount in the name of business development in the name of various (fictitious) persons. It is stated in the FIR by the informant that the aforesaid occurrences of criminal breach of trust (committed by the accused) were detected by the Inspecting Team of the Bangladesh Bank between 24.4.92 and 3.5.92 after due inspection and enquiry. 

 14. The word "banker" in section 409 of the Penal Code has not been used in the technical sense of the Banking Companies Act but signifies any person who discharges any of the functions of the customary business of banking and would also include a firm or company that carries on such business (see Nadir Ali, 1960 CrLJ 188). In the instant case from the accusation of the accused-petitioner it is clear that the accused was acting as a banker, that the accused in such capacity was entrusted by various depositors with the aforesaid various amounts of money in question or had dominion over the said amounts of money and that the accused as a banker committed the most heinous offence by dishonestly committing criminal breach of trust by misappropriating the same. 

 16. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that provision of section 497 (1) CrPC does not mean that if there is a prima facie case against the accused under section 409 of the Penal Code which is punishable with imprisonment for life, bail cannot be granted to the accused and that bail should not be refused by way of punishment. He refers to the decision in the case of Shaikh Shahidul Islam Vs. Slate, 44 DLR (AD) 192 wherein it was observed : 

 "It is not the prima facie case against the accused as held by the learned Judge but 'reasonable grounds' for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life which prohibit granting of bail under the provision referred to above...... 

 The Court's belief on the point has to rest on the accusations made in the report to the police, the nature and the credentials of the evidence which the prosecution proposes to lead in the case, and all the other relevant circumstances surrounding the occurrence." 

 In the facts of the aforesaid case of Sk. Shahidul Islam Vs. Stale, 44 DLR (AD) 192 the accused who was a Minister for Education perchance presided over a meeting regarding the purchase of a ship in the absence of the Minister for Shipping, the Appellate Division held that it is difficult to be satisfied about the reasonable grounds by merely looking at the allegations made in the FIR or charge-sheet. 

 17. In the case of Nisar Ahmed Vs. The Slate, 23 DLR (SC) 41 in dealing with the interpretation of the provision made in section 497 CrPC the Supreme Court of Pakistan observed, 

 “........When a prima facie case has been made, it cannot be said that in spite of it, there are no reasonable grounds for believing the accused to be guilty. It is, however, open to an accused person to pray for his bail even after his commitment, by showing that his commitment has not been made to rest on any reasonable grounds, 

 ............In a situation like this, in order to justify the continued detention of the accused in prison, it would be for the higher Courts to see whether the commitment order does disclose that satisfaction of mind on the part of the Committing Magistrate, which is necessary for committing an accused person for trial on the basis that a prima facie case for an offence punishable with death or transportation has been made out against him." 

 18. In the instant case we have already shown that the information was lodged by the informant who is a duly authorised officer of the Bangladesh Bank and that the said incriminating facts against the accused-petitioner was disclosed in the FIR by the informant after due inquiry by the inspecting team of the Bangladesh Bank in the aforesaid relevant branches of the BCI Limited. There are thus reasonable grounds for this Court believing that the accused-petitioner Mustafizur Rahman has been guilty of committing criminal breach of trust of a very heinous nature in the facts and circumstances of the case in respect of the aforesaid amounts of money after having got dominion over it by withdrawing the same in various ways in the name of his accomplices and that the said offence is punishable with imprisonment for life. The learned Sessions Judge has thin lightly rejected the petition for bail of the petitioner and we find no reason to grant the prayer for bail.
